abstract: Local curation note, not a verified literature excerpt: metallic calcium can react with air/moisture during handling, so pre-sealing exposure is a plausible loss pathway if exposure was significant. The supplied record only indicates brief possible exposure, not enough to prove primacy.

abstract: Local curation note, not a verified literature excerpt: calcium can be mobile or lost from a hot melt/ampoule region under some growth conditions; deposit or residual flux analysis would be needed to test this mechanism directly.

title: Local curation note: container or contaminant reaction
abstract: Local curation note, not a verified literature excerpt: reactive calcium may interact with crucible materials, ampoule surfaces, oxide contamination, or residual impurities. A changed liner or post-growth container analysis would be needed to elevate this above a possibility.

title: Local curation note: Fe-Al or Al-rich competing phases
abstract: Local curation note, not a verified literature excerpt: Fe-Al and Al-rich competing phases can plausibly dominate recovered crystals when the target Ca-containing phase does not form or Ca is depleted. XRD comparison against candidate Fe-Al phases is needed.

title: Local curation note: EDX limitation
abstract: Local curation note, not a verified literature excerpt: EDX samples a local interaction volume and can miss bulk composition differences, surface depletion, roughness effects, or small inclusions. Bulk composition or WDS/cross-section mapping is needed before concluding true bulk Ca absence.

title: Local curation note: bulk composition discriminator
abstract: Local curation note: ICP-OES or ICP-MS would directly test whether recovered material is truly Ca-poor in bulk, distinguishing a real Ca-loss/competing-phase outcome from a surface-sensitive EDX undercount before more mechanism-specific follow-up.

title: Local curation note: residual flux and ampoule-wall deposits
abstract: Local curation note: analyzing residual flux and ampoule-wall deposits can test whether Ca transported away from the crystals during heating or decanting, but it is most useful after establishing whether the crystals are truly bulk Ca-poor.

title: Local curation note: quench series
abstract: Local curation note: an intermediate quench series with phase characterization could identify when competing phases appear, but it requires more synthesis effort than a first bulk-composition check.
